title: Post-hoc derivation of a canonical motion-aware curvature risk candidate
question: Can a previous-frame-only local curvature estimate separate transported signal gradient from bilinear interpolation uncertainty on the failed D12.8 motion evidence while remaining byte-identical across Python and Node?
decisionRole: candidate selection only; this derivation may not support production or revise any prior verdict

candidate.name: Q30_PREVIOUS_CURVATURE_X4
candidate.inputDomain: D12.8 structurally valid radius-2 pixels; RGB and motion are read only from the previous frame and current Blender Vector; current RGB is forbidden from the decision
candidate.support: the 4x4 previous-frame rectangle [x0-1,x0+2] by [y0-1,y0+2] is in bounds, has one exact Object Index and alpha greater than 0.999

colorFixedPoint.requirement: every previous float32 RGB sample multiplied by 2^30 is an exact integer in the declared [0,1] derivation domain

motionFixedPoint.requirement: the fractional part of q=(x+Vector.X,y-Vector.Y), multiplied by 2^24, is an exact integer

candidate.curvature: Mx is the per-channel maximum absolute horizontal second difference at x0 and x0+1 on rows y0 and y0+1; My is the analogous vertical maximum at y0 and y0+1 on columns x0 and x0+1; all colors are signed Q30 integers
candidate.reconstruction: unchanged four-tap float64 bilinear sum followed by one float32 cast; reconstruction is measured but not an input to the risk decision
candidate.fallback: ineligible or risk-rejected pixels copy current float32 RGBA exactly in the future holdout

requirements: freeze unseen Blender 5.2 fixtures, transforms, materials, resolutions, tool hashes and verdict mapping before any formal render
recompute structural validity rather than importing D12.8 masks
measure predicted-depth agreement only on analytically valid history and count expected depth rejection in a separate domain
require non-empty useful coverage for every moving analytic owner
retain exact current-RGBA fallback and zero false acceptance of invalid history
treat this D12.8-derived candidate and both thresholds as fixed; no post-hoc widening

nonClaims: D12.9-D1 is post-hoc on D12.8 and is not a holdout.
It does not show that finite second differences are a mathematical upper bound for arbitrary rendered signals.
It does not validate curved or deforming geometry, path-traced lighting, transparency, motion blur, depth of field, denoising, cinematic quality or production use.
Only a future preregistered fresh Blender 5.2 experiment may test generalization.
